section_summary: This section documents the planning, funding, and staffing of the State Department's project to microfilm Japanese Foreign Office archives in Tokyo in collaboration with SCAP and the Library of Congress. It also addresses the custody, screening, and disposition of Japanese diplomatic and consular documents located in Washington, Italy, and Latin America, as well as Dutch inquiries regarding captured Pacific war records. Key staffing actions trace the selection and clearance of Glenn W. Shaw and Thomas C. Smith to carry out the microfilming operation after Delmer Brown was deemed unacceptable by occupation authorities.

subfiles.about: The Netherlands State Institute of War Documentation inquires whether the Washington Document Center holds records concerning the Netherlands and Netherlands East Indies during World War II.
subfiles.from: Drs L. de Jong, Acting Director, Netherlands State Institute of War Documentation
subfiles.summary: Requests access to examine and photocopy World War II records relating to the Netherlands and the Indies.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Records in the Washington Document Center
subfiles.to: Central Intelligence Group, Office of Collection and Dissemination

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research submits questions for John R. Shively regarding the condition and feasibility of microfilming Japanese Foreign Office archives.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Lists confidential questions for John R. Shively concerning the completeness, security, and microfilming feasibility of Japanese Foreign Office archives.
subfiles.title: Questions Concerning Japanese Foreign Office Documents
subfiles.to: Thomas N. Simpson, Reorientation Branch, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army

subfiles.about: The Division of Research for Far East requests a loan of Japanese Embassy records for scanning and translation selection.
subfiles.from: Jack W. Lydman, Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.summary: Requests on loan the remaining Japanese official documents assembled by Mr. Okami for scanning and translation evaluation.
subfiles.title: Japanese Official Documents Discovered at Japanese Embassy, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services

subfiles.about: SCAP reports survey findings on preserved and destroyed Japanese Foreign Office documents across imperial eras and tribunal holdings.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports document counts of preserved and destroyed Foreign Office records, tribunal holdings, and general completeness of diplomatic files.
subfiles.title: Survey of Japanese Foreign Office Documents
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research seeks clarification on document statistics and discrepancies regarding Foreign Office archive losses.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether reported archive figures refer to individual pages or files and queries discrepancies with Atcheson's previous loss estimates.
subfiles.title: Clarification of Japanese Foreign Office Document Statistics
subfiles.to: William J. Sebald, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: Special Agent Hall reports on the transfer offer of 81 reels of nitrate motion picture film from the Japanese Embassy to the Library of Congress.
subfiles.from: John R. Hall, Special Agent, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.summary: Reports informing the Library of Congress that 81 nitrate film reels from the Japanese Embassy are available for acquisition.
subfiles.title: Films, German and Japanese Embassies
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Security and Investigation

subfiles.about: The Office of the Assistant Secretary discusses Netherlands requests concerning SEATIC documents destroyed by PACMIRS and pending National Archives transfers.
subfiles.from: P. P. Claxton, Office of the Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas
subfiles.summary: Recommends informing Minister Reuchlin that destruction of SEATIC documents is under investigation and transfer to Archives will take six months.
subfiles.title: Statement to Minister Reuchlin re SEATIC Documents
subfiles.to: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo notifies the Department that microfilms of Foreign Office document catalog lists were dispatched to Army Intelligence.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports that nine volumes of Foreign Office catalog microfilms were forwarded by G-2 to the Director of Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Microfilms of Japanese Foreign Office Document Lists
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo clarifies statistical discrepancies regarding destroyed Foreign Office archives, library materials, and IMTFE document disposition.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Explains discrepancies in Foreign Office volume counts and library losses, advising coordination with Army Intelligence regarding prosecution documents.
subfiles.title: Status and Statistics of Japanese Foreign Office Archives and Library
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Professor Delmer M. Brown inquires about access to Japanese diplomatic archives and the possibility of cooperative microfilming during his upcoming trip.
subfiles.from: Delmer M. Brown, University of California, Berkeley
subfiles.summary: Inquires about access to Japanese diplomatic records and proposes microfilming or cooperating on research during a trip to Japan.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Concerning Access to Japanese Diplomatic Documents
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research responds to Delmer Brown concerning the projected publication program on Japanese diplomatic papers.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Informs Brown of the pending diplomatic papers project and expresses interest in consulting him during his travel to Japan.
subfiles.title: Proposed Research Program on Japanese Diplomatic Papers
subfiles.to: Delmer M. Brown, University of California, Berkeley

subfiles.about: The Division of Protective Services transmits a list and receipt of 81 Japanese government documents transferred on loan to DRF.
subfiles.from: K. Okami, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.summary: Transmits a signed receipt and translated inventory of 81 Japanese official documents transferred to the Division of Research for Far East.
subfiles.title: Transfer of Japanese Official Documents to DRF
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services

subfiles.about: The Central Intelligence Agency circulates an inventory of records from the former Japanese Embassy in Italy to determine disposal or transfer.
subfiles.from: C. F. Heney, Acting Chief, Requirements Branch, CIA
subfiles.summary: Circulates an itemized list of 25 document groups from the former Japanese Embassy in Rome to assess agency retention interests.
subfiles.title: Documents from Former Japanese Embassy in Italy, Disposition of
subfiles.to: Department of State and Military Intelligence Directors

subfiles.about: The Department of State recommends returning private Rome embassy records to Italy and transferring official archives to Japan.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Recommends returning personal property records to Italy and sending general official archives to Japan under international usage.
subfiles.title: Disposition of Documents from Former Japanese Embassy in Italy
subfiles.to: C. F. Heney, Acting Chief, Requirements Branch, CIA

subfiles.about: The Division of Protective Services advises that enemy diplomatic archives should be preserved intact rather than accessioned into US National Archives.
subfiles.from: E. Williams III, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.summary: Recommends personal files be returned to Italy and remaining embassy records delivered to SCAP for the Japanese Government.
subfiles.title: Position on Disposition of Japanese Embassy Records in Italy
subfiles.to: Kemp, Reference Division

subfiles.about: The CIA Map Branch acknowledges the receipt on loan of 112 map sheets from the Japanese Embassy collection.
subfiles.from: Arthur L. Burt, Map Branch, CIA
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt on loan of 112 map sheets from the Japanese Embassy collection pending translation and detailed cataloguing.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Receipt of Maps
subfiles.to: Assistant Chief, Division of Protective Services

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research proposes reducing the Japanese War Documents Project to a minimal microfilming operation.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Explains budget reductions and proposes sending a small microfilming team of two operators and one supervisor to Tokyo under SCAP auspices.
subfiles.title: Proposal for Reduced Japanese War Documents Microfilm Project
subfiles.to: William J. Sebald, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo reviews operational considerations, Allied sensitivities, archive classification categories, and workload estimates for microfilming.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Assesses microfilming feasibility, warns of Allied sensitivities regarding archive access, and transmits file classifications showing over four million pages to film.
subfiles.title: Feasibility and Logistics of Foreign Office Microfilming Project
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State urgently queries USPOLAD Tokyo regarding personnel requirements, document supervision, and office controls for the research project.
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Urgently requests decisions on whether a two-scholar team is acceptable and whether adequate supervisory control can be maintained.
subfiles.title: Urgent Inquiries on Foreign Office Research Project
subfiles.to: USPOLAD Tokyo

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo references its letter of June 1 as providing full answers to Department inquiries regarding the War Documents Project.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: States that questions regarding the war documents research project are answered in Sebald's letter of June 1.
subfiles.title: Reply to Department Inquiries on War Documents Project
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Central Records certifies a replacement record sheet for San Salvador Airgram A-158.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records (DC/R)
subfiles.summary: Designates an attached copy of San Salvador Airgram A-158 as the permanent official record copy for central files.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Copy Form for San Salvador Airgram A-158
subfiles.to: Central Files

subfiles.about: The American Embassy in San Salvador reports the physical deterioration of stored German and Japanese archives and requests disposition instructions.
subfiles.from: Albert F. Nufer, American Embassy San Salvador
subfiles.summary: Reports severe mildew and insect damage to enemy archives stored at the Chancery and requests ultimate disposition instructions.
subfiles.title: Condition and Disposition of German and Japanese Archives in San Salvador
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Department instructs the Embassy in San Salvador to maintain deteriorating German and Japanese archives on premises pending future decisions.
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instructs the Embassy to continue holding enemy archives on premises despite unavoidable storage deterioration until international disposition is decided.
subfiles.title: Instructions Concerning Enemy Archives in San Salvador
subfiles.to: American Embassy San Salvador

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum fragment comments on a draft SANACC paper regarding trusteeship of Japanese diplomatic properties.
subfiles.from: Unknown
subfiles.summary: Suggests revisions to a draft SANACC paper regarding four-power trusteeships and the preservation of Japanese diplomatic properties abroad.
subfiles.title: Comments on Draft SANACC Paper on Japanese Diplomatic Properties (Fragment)
subfiles.to: Unknown

subfiles.about: Robert S. Schwantes inquires about the proposed Japanese archives program and submits his academic and Japanese language qualifications.
subfiles.from: Robert S. Schwantes
subfiles.summary: Inquires about recruitment for the proposed Japanese archives exploitation program and submits details of his background and language training.
subfiles.title: Inquiry and Application Concerning Japanese Documents Project
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research advises Robert Schwantes on the uncertain status and limited scope of the Japanese documents program.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Explains funding shortages have reduced the project to microfilming and notes Schwantes's qualifications for future consideration.
subfiles.title: Status of Japanese War Documents Project and Recruitment
subfiles.to: Robert S. Schwantes

subfiles.about: The Division of Eastern European Affairs reviews Soviet policy implications regarding the transfer of legal custody of Japanese properties to host governments.
subfiles.from: Edward L. Freers, Division of Eastern European Affairs
subfiles.summary: Finds no objection regarding Soviet relations to transferring custody of Japanese property to host governments, suggesting replacing Colombia as an example.
subfiles.title: Legal Custody of Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives and Property
subfiles.to: Llewellyn E. Thompson, Division of Eastern European Affairs

subfiles.about: The Division of Eastern European Affairs discusses trusteeship examples and clears documentation on Japanese diplomatic archives and properties.
subfiles.from: Llewellyn E. Thompson, Division of Eastern European Affairs
subfiles.summary: Initializes papers regarding custody of Japanese diplomatic properties, noting after discussion that the paper can proceed without amending the Colombia example.
subfiles.title: Clearance of Papers on Japanese Diplomatic Archives and Property
subfiles.to: Samuel Boykin, Division of Consular Affairs

subfiles.about: Custodian Okami reports discovering approximately one thousand letters and diplomatic records of Ambassador Saito in the basement of the FEC.
subfiles.from: K. Okami, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.summary: Reports discovering Ambassador Saito's correspondence in the FEC basement and segregating subversive propaganda offer letters from American citizens.
subfiles.title: Additional Japanese Documents Found in the Basement of the FEC
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary of State inquires whether SCAP can provide two microfilm operators for the Foreign Office project.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Urges an early reply regarding the microfilm project and asks whether SCAP can furnish two operators.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Concerning Provision of Microfilm Operators by SCAP
subfiles.to: USPOLAD Tokyo

subfiles.about: Professor Delmer M. Brown reports encouraging prospects for leave of absence to participate in the Japanese War Documents Project.
subfiles.from: Delmer M. Brown, University of California, Berkeley
subfiles.summary: Reports positive indications for academic leave to lead the documents project upon receiving definite word from the Department.
subfiles.title: Leave Prospects for Japanese War Documents Project
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research informs Delmer Brown of Library of Congress funding and offers him the supervisory position.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Reports securing $30,000 from the Library of Congress and outlines plans to offer Brown the top P-7 supervisory position pending Tokyo's approval.
subfiles.title: Progress of Japanese War Documents Project and Offer of Leadership
subfiles.to: Delmer M. Brown, University of California, Berkeley

subfiles.about: The Librarian of Congress proposes transferring $30,000 and microfilm cameras to the State Department to copy Japanese Foreign Office records.
subfiles.from: Luther H. Evans, Librarian of Congress
subfiles.summary: Proposes transferring a $30,000 working fund and three cameras to the State Department to obtain microfilms of Japanese Foreign Office records.
subfiles.title: Proposal to Finance Microfilming of Japanese Foreign Office Records
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: A draft second page outlines terms regarding declassification and access for microfilms funded by the Library of Congress.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Draft second page specifying terms for handling restricted film and reserving State Department research access.
subfiles.title: Terms for Acceptance of Library of Congress Working Fund (Draft Page 2)
subfiles.to: Luther H. Evans, Librarian of Congress

subfiles.about: The Department of State agrees to accept the Library of Congress working fund subject to specified administrative and declassification terms.
subfiles.from: John E. Peurifoy, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: First page of letter agreeing to accept the $30,000 fund and cameras to support two professional supervisors and supplies.
subfiles.title: Acceptance of Library of Congress Working Fund (Page 1)
subfiles.to: Luther H. Evans, Librarian of Congress

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research inquires whether George Everett Potter remains interested in work with the Japanese documents project.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether Potter remains interested in potential employment with the Japanese War Documents Project.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Availability for Japanese War Documents Project
subfiles.to: George Everett Potter

subfiles.about: The concluding page of the Department's letter to the Librarian of Congress transmits standard voucher Form 1080 for fund transfer.
subfiles.from: John E. Peurifoy, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Second page of letter requesting technical specifications and enclosing Standard Form 1080 to transfer funds from the Treasury.
subfiles.title: Acceptance of Library of Congress Working Fund (Page 2)
subfiles.to: Luther H. Evans, Librarian of Congress

subfiles.about: The Library of Congress transmits the executed transfer voucher, a check for $30,000, and camera equipment details.
subfiles.from: David C. Mearns, Acting Librarian of Congress
subfiles.summary: Transmits executed transfer voucher, $30,000 check, technical specifications, and confirms three portable microfilm cameras are ready.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Working Fund Check and Microfilm Specifications
subfiles.to: John E. Peurifoy, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research requests Edwin O. Reischauer's assistance in finding a qualified candidate in Tokyo after Brown's rejection.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Explains Delmer Brown's rejection due to press publicity and asks Reischauer to recommend a qualified scholar in Tokyo to head the project.
subfiles.title: Request for Assistance in Recruiting Project Director
subfiles.to: Edwin O. Reischauer, Headquarters, Far Eastern Command

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary queries whether Glenn W. Shaw would be acceptable to SCAP as P-7 head of the Foreign Office documents project.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether Glenn W. Shaw of the Navy Language School would be acceptable to head the Tokyo project.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Concerning Acceptability of Glenn W. Shaw
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Department of the Army transmits a priority query to SCAP regarding candidate acceptability for the Foreign Office archives project.
subfiles.from: Department of the Army
subfiles.summary: Relays State Department message inquiring whether proposed candidates are acceptable to SCAP for the archives project.
subfiles.title: Staff Message Concerning Acceptability of Personnel for Documents Project
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Acting Secretary inquires whether Tom C. Smith of Stanford University is acceptable as the second professional for the project.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether Tom C. Smith of Stanford is acceptable as the second professional member of the Tokyo project.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Concerning Acceptability of Tom C. Smith
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo notifies the Department that Tom C. Smith is acceptable for the documents project.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Confirms Tom C. Smith is acceptable to SCAP and clearance arrangements will be made upon request.
subfiles.title: Acceptability of Tom C. Smith for Documents Project
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State advises that Tom C. Smith has been cleared by State and reports that Shaw is en route to Japan aboard the Gaffey.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Notifies SCAP that Smith is cleared, requests theater entry clearance, and states Shaw is en route aboard the transport Gaffey.
subfiles.title: Travel and Clearance Status of Smith and Shaw
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research consults USPOLAD Tokyo on transportation and diplomatic housing rules for project personnel and wives.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Discusses financial and transport problems regarding travel for wives and asks whether SCAP can provide housing and accept Dr. Smith.
subfiles.title: Travel Arrangements and Housing for Project Personnel
subfiles.to: William J. Sebald, Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research discusses travel schedules, equipment shipments, and camera operator training with USPOLAD Tokyo.
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Reviews housing restrictions, notes dispatch of three cameras and film rolls, and suggests Signal Corps train Japanese machine operators.
subfiles.title: Operational Preparations and Personnel Dispatch for Microfilming Project
subfiles.to: William J. Sebald, Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo confirms project clearances for Shaw and Smith, explains Brown's press controversy, and assesses camera availability in Japan.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Confirms project approval for Shaw and Smith, attributes Brown's rejection to press statements, and reviews Library of Congress equipment in Japan.
subfiles.title: Project Clearance and Equipment Status in Tokyo
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo explains GHQ billeting regulations, housing waiting lists, and credit rules precluding immediate dependent entry.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that POLAD is part of GHQ rather than a diplomatic mission, detailing billeting credit rules and housing delays for wives.
subfiles.title: Housing Regulations and Waiting Lists in Tokyo
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Chief, Division of Historical Policy Research

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State notifies SCAP that Glenn Shaw is cleared and ready to depart, requesting entry clearance and Army transport for his wife.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: States Shaw is ready to leave for Tokyo and requests SCAP clearance and Army transportation for Shaw and his wife.
subfiles.title: Clearance and Transportation Request for Glenn Shaw
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo confirms Glenn Shaw is cleared for entry into Japan but notes clearance for his wife must await his arrival.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Confirms Shaw is cleared for entry, stating clearance for his wife cannot be considered until his arrival.
subfiles.title: Entry Clearance for Glenn Shaw
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo notifies the Department that Tom C. Smith is cleared for entry into Japan and requests his firm arrival date.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports that Tom C. Smith is cleared for entry into Japan and requests his firm estimated arrival date.
subfiles.title: Entry Clearance for Tom C. Smith
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State informs SCAP that Tom C. Smith is en route to Tokyo with an estimated arrival date of April 10.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs SCAP that Tom C. Smith is en route to Tokyo with an estimated time of arrival of April 10.
subfiles.title: Travel Notification and Arrival Date for Tom C. Smith
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Division of Historical Policy Research requests telegraphic authorization of quarters allowances for civilian personnel in Tokyo and Bletchley.
subfiles.from: Division of Historical Policy Research
subfiles.summary: Submits telegrams authorizing quarters allowances for research personnel stationed in Tokyo and Bletchley, England.
subfiles.title: Quarters Allowance for RE Civilian Personnel Stationed in Tokyo and Bletchley
subfiles.to: John E. Peurifoy, Assistant Secretary for Administration

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State authorizes standardized quarters allowance payments for Glenn W. Shaw and Thomas C. Smith in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Authorizes annual quarters allowances up to $1,200 for Shaw and $900 for Smith payable from State working fund appropriations.
subfiles.title: Authorization of Quarters Allowance for Shaw and Smith
subfiles.to: SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: Central Records certifies a replacement record sheet for a Tokyo despatch or telegram dated May 5, 1949.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records (DC/R)
subfiles.summary: Designates an attached replacement copy of a Tokyo communication as the permanent official record copy for central files.
subfiles.title: Replacement Record Copy Form for Tokyo Communication 145
subfiles.to: Central Files
